source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Wisconsin technical college opens $3.5M dental clinic for hygiene and assistant training
summary: Mid-State Technical College has opened a $3.5 million dental clinic in Wisconsin Rapids to support its new dental hygiene and dental assistant programs. The program will take up to 10 students in each field per semester, and the clinic includes simulation labs, dental imaging rooms and dental chairs. Hygiene students are currently in entry-level courses and will start hygiene program classes in the fall.
why: The new training capacity adds to the pipeline of hygienists and dental assistants, and the college credited feedback and engagement from the local dental community, which may create opportunities for practices to partner with the program.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Five dentists take on new leadership roles across DSOs, schools and associations
summary: Smile Brands promoted Jason Genta, DDS, to senior vice president of clinical operations. Thomas Paumier, DDS, was installed as the 163rd president of the American Dental Association, and Nova Southeastern University named Andres Pinto, DDS, DMD, dean of its College of Dental Medicine effective Jan. 2. The roundup also notes that Marcelo Araujo, DDS, PhD, was elected to the FDI World Dental Federation's Science Committee and that the Minnesota Dental Association installed John Noack, DDS, as president for the 2026-27 term.
why: Changes in leadership at DSOs, dental schools and professional associations can shift the clinical direction, education priorities and policy agenda that affect how practicing dentists work and train the next generation.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Videa's dental AI imaging tools will reach Canadian practices via ClearDent
summary: Boston-based Videa has partnered with British Columbia-based ClearDent, a dental practice management platform, to bring Videa's AI imaging into ClearDent's software in Canada. Radiographs captured in ClearDent can be automatically analyzed by Videa's AI, with findings meant to support patient education and treatment acceptance. Videa is the first AI imaging partner to launch through ClearDent's Embedded Experience program.
why: Dentists using ClearDent in Canada may gain access to AI-assisted radiograph analysis inside their existing practice management system, which could affect how findings are explained to patients and how treatment is presented.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Ranking of US dental schools by 2025-26 graduate count released by ADA data
summary: Based on American Dental Association data for the 2025-26 academic year, New York University led the list of dental schools by number of graduates, followed by Tufts University and Boston University. The article lists the top 10 schools, with the ranking ending at Midwestern University with 142 graduates.
why: Dentists and dental specialists considering where to recruit new graduates or where to train may find this graduate-volume data useful for understanding the pipeline of incoming dentists.

headline: Scoping review sorts evidence on 3D-printed versus thermoformed aligners and retainers
summary: A recent scoping review examined studies on thermoformed and 3D-printed orthodontic appliances and their materials. It notes that laboratory, ageing and safety findings are often presented as if they matter as much as patient studies, which can leave clinicians relying on manufacturers' claims. The review aims to clarify what can be concluded about appliance performance and which clinical questions remain open.
why: Dentists who prescribe or fabricate aligners and retainers can use this review to judge how much weight to give lab data versus clinical studies when choosing between appliance types.

headline: Reexamining tissue-level implants for front-tooth aesthetic cases
summary: A new clinical article revisits the use of tissue-level implants in anterior restorations, where their role remains debated. The debate centers on limited control over the emergence profile and the possibility of implant collar exposure. The authors argue for their use by examining possible biological and mechanical benefits of the design.
why: Clinicians placing implants in visible front-tooth sites may find this a useful reference when weighing tissue-level designs against alternatives for aesthetic outcomes.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Specialized Dental Partners reaches 200 partnerships across 37 states
summary: Franklin, Tennessee-based Specialized Dental Partners has marked its 200th partnership. The DSO began in 2018 as US Endo Partners, focused only on endodontists, then expanded into other specialties and was renamed in 2023. According to the company, its network now includes more than 450 doctors and 2,500 team members across 37 states.
why: Growth of specialty-focused DSOs like this one signals increasing consolidation among specialty practices, which may affect how independent specialists weigh partnership options.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Former Aspen Group sales executive named COO of Southern Orthodontic Partners
summary: Nashville-based Southern Orthodontic Partners has appointed Sarah Sharfstein as its chief operating officer. She previously held leadership roles over eight years at The Aspen Group, most recently as vice president of sales enablement and sales effectiveness, and spent more than a decade at Align Technology. The DSO supports more than 120 practices across the southern U.S.
why: The hire of a leader with sales and operations experience from large dental companies signals how DSOs are staffing their management teams to support their growing networks of practices.

headline: Videa's AI imaging joins ClearDent software for Canadian dental practices
summary: Videa and ClearDent announced a partnership that brings Videa's AI-assisted radiographic analysis into ClearDent Imaging. Radiographs captured in ClearDent can be analyzed automatically and securely, with findings shown alongside patient images and treatment information. Videa is the first AI imaging partner to launch through ClearDent's Embedded Experience framework.
why: Dentists using ClearDent in Canada may be able to review AI-assisted imaging findings within their existing software, which could help them explain findings and recommended care to patients more clearly.

headline: China's second dental implant bulk procurement round weighs quality alongside price
summary: Chinese healthcare authorities are putting more weight on product quality in the second round of volume-based procurement for dental implants and related consumables, which launched on 28 September. Sichuan province is leading the implant contract renewals and Shaanxi province is leading those for orthodontic products. Manufacturers that offer a competitive mix of price and quality could receive larger procurement volumes.
why: For dentists and practices sourcing implants in or from China, procurement rules that reward quality as well as price may shape which implant brands are available and at what cost.

headline: Oryx Dental Software Wins 2026 Inc. Power Partner Award
summary: Oryx Dental Software, a cloud-based and AI-powered dental practice management platform, was named a 2026 winner of the Inc. Power Partner Awards. The annual honor recognizes B2B companies that help entrepreneurs and businesses grow through services such as technology, compliance, and marketing. The excerpt notes Oryx was founded by a dentist and combines clinical workflows, patient records, scheduling, billing, and AI tools in one platform.
why: For a practicing dentist, this is a vendor recognition rather than a clinical finding, but it highlights practice management software that aims to reduce workflow complexity so teams can focus on patient care.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Dental M&A deal volume falls 27% from a year earlier in Q3 2026
summary: Levin Associates reported 51 dental transactions in the third quarter of 2026, which it said accounted for 49% of all physician medical group mergers and acquisitions. Dental deal volume fell 7% from the second quarter and 27% from the third quarter of 2025. DSOs made up 30 of the deals, including 16 by private equity-backed DSOs, with Imagen Dental Partners and Heartland Dental among the most active.
why: A slowdown in dental deal activity, especially among DSOs and private equity-backed groups, signals shifting competition and buyer interest that could affect practice sale and partnership options.

headline: Dentsply Sirona Reports Progress Five Years Into Its BEYOND Sustainability Strategy
summary: Dentsply Sirona is marking five years of its BEYOND sustainability strategy, which is built on the pillars Healthy Planet, Healthy Smiles, and Healthy Business. The company says it has made strong progress toward its 2025 goals, has exceeded its target of 25 million smiles, and has cut Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity by more than 30% against the 2019 baseline. It is also setting new ambitions for 2030.
why: For a practice, the manufacturer's push on reduced packaging waste and longer equipment lifespan through service and repair may affect how dental products and equipment are sourced, maintained, and replaced.

headline: National Norwegian study examines quality of life among oral health professionals
summary: A British Dental Journal article reports a national study of professional quality of life among oral health professionals in Norway. The excerpt contains only the title and citation, so its findings are not available here.
why: Dentists and their teams may find this study useful for understanding how working conditions affect professional well-being across the oral health workforce.

headline: Solventum launches redesigned Filtek Matrix system for conservative anterior composites
summary: Solventum has made available a next-generation Filtek Matrix restorative system, built on matrix technology first introduced in 2022. The redesign adds a new delivery system meant to make placement and cleanup more efficient, and it works with a digital workflow and Solventum's restorative materials. Through its Clarity Portal planning platform, clinicians receive patient-specific treatment plans, and a customized 3D-printed matrix is then used to guide placement of Filtek restoratives.
why: Dentists placing anterior composites may find that a more efficient matrix delivery and cleanup process could save chair time and support conservative, natural-looking restorations for patients.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Vitana Pediatric & Orthodontic Partners adds Hollis Orthodontics in Louisiana
summary: Vitana Pediatric & Orthodontic Partners, a Fort Lauderdale-based group, has added Hollis Orthodontics in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to its network, according to an October 19 LinkedIn post. The practice is led by Bryan Hollis, DDS. The group, which supports practices in 10 states, earlier added Saratoga Investment Corp. as a debt financing partner in June to fund its growth.
why: It shows continued consolidation by dental support organizations, which may matter to independent orthodontic and pediatric practices weighing affiliation or financing options.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: WVU School of Dentistry receives $15M federal award for renovations and equipment
summary: The West Virginia University School of Dentistry in Morgantown received a $15 million Congressionally Directed Spending award through the Health Resources and Services Administration. Sen. Shelley Capito, who helped secure the funding, announced it in an October 20 release, and the money will go toward dental school renovations and equipment purchases. The school had also received $12.6 million in 2024 for an expansion and renovation project.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Five dentists weigh in on how vertical integration will reshape dental care
summary: Becker's Dental Review gathered views from five dental leaders on vertical integration, prompted by Optum's recently awarded $30 billion VA dental contract. The article notes that payers and large health systems are moving deeper into dentistry, and that dental executives expect financial performance to determine which practices survive. The excerpt also cites VA figures showing more than 800,000 veterans received dental care through the VA in fiscal year 2025.
why: Dentists should expect growing pressure from large payers and health systems, which could affect practice independence, reimbursement, and referral patterns, so financial planning and strategy matter more.

source: Becker’s Dental Review – DSO + Dental News
headline: Unified Patent Court sides with Align Technology in Angelalign infringement case
summary: The Unified Patent Court ruled that Angelalign's aligner systems using its Torque Ridges feature infringe Align Technology's Power Ridge patent, and it rejected Angelalign's challenges to the patent's validity. Angelalign must stop offering the systems in 17 countries, recall and destroy infringing products, and pay damages. The ruling can still be appealed, and a separate Chinese court earlier found Angelalign's MasterForce and ATreat systems infringed Align's patent rights.
why: This ongoing dispute between two clear-aligner makers could affect which aligner products are available in Europe and how competition in the market plays out for practices that offer clear aligners.

headline: Dr. Silverman on why the IEEM approach builds patient trust in cosmetic dentistry
summary: In his weekly reflection, Harvey N. Silverman argues that successful cosmetic practices using the IEEM System (Inform, Educate, Empower & Motivate) help patients feel comfortable asking questions and considering options. He says team members should see their role as informing and educating patients rather than selling, so patients can make better decisions. He concludes that reducing uncertainty tends to reduce patient resistance.
why: The piece suggests that framing cosmetic treatment as education rather than sales may help patients feel less pressured and more willing to explore options, which bears on how a practice presents treatment.

headline: AAE Launches Online Marketplace for Endodontic Products and Services
summary: The American Association of Endodontists has launched AAE Marketplace, an online platform at marketplace.aae.org that lists more than 140 solution providers serving endodontists. Members can browse company profiles, explore products and services, access special offers and educational content, and share recommendations.
why: Endodontists and other practitioners now have a specialty-focused place to compare vendors and products, and companies gain another way to reach members beyond annual meetings, trade shows, and traditional advertising.

headline: Sodium Trimetaphosphate Shows Promise for Enamel Protection in Toothpaste Studies
summary: A 2022 Clinical Oral Investigations study found that a toothpaste with 200 ppm fluoride, 0.2% sodium trimetaphosphate (STMP), 16% xylitol, and 4% erythritol gave greater protection against early enamel erosion and better surface-hardness recovery than all other tested formulas, including one with the standard 1,100 ppm fluoride. A 2021 Journal of Dentistry study with 14 volunteers wearing enamel specimens reported that the same combination produced the lowest enamel mineral loss and changed biofilm composition compared with the 1,100 ppm fluoride formula.
why: These early findings suggest phosphate and polyol additives might help fluoride toothpastes do more at lower fluoride levels, which could be worth watching as dentists discuss preventive options with patients, though the excerpt is from a promotional-leaning source and the studies are limited in scope.

headline: Henry Schein to release Q3 2026 results on November 3
summary: Henry Schein will publish its third-quarter 2026 financial results before the stock market opens on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A live webcast of the earnings call will begin at 8:00 AM Eastern, with a replay posted on the company's website afterward. CEO Fred Lowery, CFO Ronald N. South, and senior financial advisor Emmanuel Caprais are scheduled to speak on the call.

headline: Guide Outlines Financing Options and Common Loan Mistakes for Dentists
summary: A guest column by a business development executive at a dental and medical funding firm walks dentists through practice financing before they take on a loan. It covers what to expect, the key questions to ask, and mistakes that can cost practice owners a significant amount over the life of a loan. The excerpt also explains that lenders often treat dental practices differently from other small businesses, with dedicated programs offering features such as little or no money down and longer repayment terms.
why: Dentists planning to buy, start, or upgrade a practice may get better loan terms by understanding dental-specific lending programs and comparing offers carefully before committing.

headline: Podcast on dental evacuation system maintenance, biofilm, and mercury from amalgam
summary: In an episode of Dentistry Today's TEN @ 10 hosted by Dr. Paul Feuerstein, infection control specialist Lori Serna-Pate discusses maintaining evacuation and suction systems. The conversation covers purging versus end-of-day line cleaning, how biofilm and amalgam mercury can affect these systems, and amalgam separators. It also touches on Solmetex cleaning products and training the whole dental team on these procedures.
why: Evacuation system cleaning is an often-overlooked area, and the episode suggests that clear protocols and team-wide training can improve consistency and compliance in the office.

headline: Dietary patterns linked to dental caries in postmenopausal women
summary: A British Dental Journal article published online examines the association between dietary patterns and dental caries experience among postmenopausal women. The excerpt is limited to the title and publication details, so specific findings are not available.
why: Diet may be a factor in caries risk for postmenopausal patients, so dentists may want to review the full paper for dietary counseling points once it is accessible.

headline: Systemic disease burden in adults 40+ attending a UK dental hospital studied via linked records
summary: A cross-sectional study published in the British Dental Journal examined the burden of systemic disease among patients aged 40 and over who attended a UK dental hospital. The authors used linked electronic health record data. The excerpt provided does not include the study's findings.
why: The study focuses on general health conditions in older dental patients, which may be relevant to how dentists consider medical history when treating this age group, though specific results are not available in the excerpt.

headline: INDICATE study to estimate undiagnosed pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes in dental primary care
summary: A British Dental Journal article published online on 19 October 2026 describes the INDICATE study, which aims to estimate how many patients in primary dental care have undiagnosed pre-diabetes or type 2 diabetes. The excerpt contains only the title and publication details, so no findings or methods are available.
why: It points to dental settings as a possible place for diabetes screening, though the excerpt gives no results yet to act on.

headline: Systemic disease common among older patients at a UK dental hospital
summary: A cross-sectional study of patients aged 40 and over at Leeds Dental Hospital, linking dental records to electronic health records from 2014 to 2023, found that about one in five patients had at least one systemic disease. Prevalence was highest in periodontal/restorative and acute dental care clinics, and patients in periodontal/restorative clinics were over three times more likely to have systemic disease than those in maxillofacial surgery clinics. The authors call for integrated information systems and care planning for medically complex dental patients.
why: Dentists treating older patients in hospital or specialist settings may see a substantial share with coexisting systemic conditions, which supports closer coordination with medical records and tailored care planning.

headline: Undiagnosed pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes common among NHS dental attendees
summary: A cross-sectional study at 13 NHS dental practices screened adults aged 40 and over without a known diagnosis using two validated diabetes risk questionnaires and point-of-care HbA1c testing. About 10% had non-diabetic hyperglycaemia (pre-diabetes) and 3% had previously undiagnosed type 2 diabetes. Both questionnaires showed good sensitivity but low specificity, and adding HbA1c testing improved specificity in a two-step pathway.
why: Dental teams, particularly when treating patients with periodontitis, may be well placed to flag undiagnosed diabetes, and a questionnaire followed by HbA1c testing offers a practical way to screen with fewer false positives.

headline: Healthier diets linked to fewer cavities in postmenopausal women, but not to progression
summary: In a study of postmenopausal women from the OsteoPerio cohort, researchers compared several dietary pattern scores with DMFT (decayed, missing, and filled teeth) counts. At baseline, higher Healthy Eating Index, Alternative Healthy Eating Index, and alternate Mediterranean Diet scores were associated with fewer missing teeth and lower DMFT scores. The researchers found no significant prospective link between diet scores and changes in missing or DMFT counts over five years.

headline: Norwegian study finds workplace factors drive strain more than vulnerable patient care
summary: A national survey of 984 Norwegian oral health professionals examined their professional quality of life, including secondary traumatic stress, burnout, and compassion satisfaction. More than half reported regularly treating vulnerable patients, and most reported moderate burnout and compassion satisfaction with low secondary traumatic stress. The authors found that psychosocial workplace factors, such as work-life balance and social support, contributed more to occupational strain than working with traumatised patients did.
why: It suggests that practice-level conditions like workload balance and team support may matter more for clinician wellbeing than the emotional demands of complex patients, pointing to where practices can focus their efforts.

headline: Parafunctional habits and TMD in children and teens: review finds weak, uncertain evidence
summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 35 cross-sectional studies examined whether parafunctional oral habits are linked to temporomandibular disorders in children and adolescents. Pooled estimates showed raised odds for some habits, including chewing and any parafunctional habit, but confidence intervals were wide and the sensitivity analysis was not robust. The authors rated the certainty of evidence as very low and concluded that the evidence does not support an association.
why: Dentists assessing young patients with jaw or muscle complaints should not assume that habits like chewing or biting cause TMD, since the evidence is very low certainty and cannot establish causation.

headline: Anterior oblique osteotomy gives better lateral mandibular angle projection than sagittal split
summary: A longitudinal cohort study compared conventional sagittal split osteotomy with anterior oblique osteotomy in orthognathic surgery patients, using pre- and postoperative CT and photographs with at least six months of follow-up. The anterior oblique technique produced a significant increase in gonial distance and a significant effect on horizontal soft-tissue projection in coronal slices, while the mandibular angle and vertical height did not differ between techniques.
why: For surgeons and clinicians planning orthognathic cases where mandibular angle definition matters, this suggests anterior oblique osteotomy may offer better lateral projection than the standard sagittal split, though the three-dimensional soft-tissue results showed no significant change.

headline: Endoscopic transcanal repair of TMJ herniation into the ear canal described in a case report
summary: The authors describe an 81-year-old man with right-sided ear pain worsened by jaw movement, initially misdiagnosed as malignant otitis externa, whose imaging showed a temporomandibular joint herniation through an anterior canal wall defect. After inflammation settled, the defect was repaired entirely endoscopically through the ear canal using layered autologous conchal cartilage and perichondrium. At 6 months the patient was asymptomatic with no recurrence, and histopathology excluded malignancy.

headline: Custom subperiosteal implants show 98.1% survival in severely atrophic jaws
summary: A retrospective study of 124 patients who received 211 custom-made titanium subperiosteal implants at a single maxillofacial unit between 2018 and 2025 reviewed complications and their management. The median follow-up was 28 months, and overall implant survival was 98.1%. Most complications were mild, with limited framework exposure in 9.5% of implants (almost all grade 1), a delayed non-suppurative oedema seen mainly in maxillary cases, and rare mechanical problems.
why: For dentists treating patients with severe jaw atrophy, this suggests a graftless subperiosteal option can achieve high survival with a mostly low-grade complication profile, though the study is single-centre and retrospective.

headline: Plate displacement common after sliding plate fixation in jaw surgery, but rarely harmful
summary: A retrospective cohort study at Pusan National University Dental Hospital reviewed 1,156 patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion who had mandibular setback by bilateral sagittal split ramus osteotomy with semirigid sliding plate fixation. Plate displacement occurred in about 21.6% of patients, and plate fracture in 1.2%, with nearly all events detected within 3 months. Neither displacement nor fracture was linked to worse subject-level outcomes such as refixation need, occlusal relapse, condylar resorption, or orthodontic treatment duration.

headline: Larger masseter muscle volume and cross-sectional area linked to late implant mechanical failure
summary: A matched case-control study of 23 implants with late mechanical failure (fixture, screw, or abutment fracture) and 92 successful controls used 3D CBCT reconstructions to measure masseter muscle volume and cross-sectional area. Greater muscle bulk was significantly associated with mechanical failure, and both measures showed good discrimination in ROC analysis, with proposed preliminary cut-off values. The authors describe the findings as exploratory and call for prospective validation before clinical use.
why: This raises the possibility that masseter muscle size measured on CBCT could eventually help flag patients at higher risk of implant fracture, though the cut-offs are not ready for routine clinical use.

headline: Screw access hole size affects fit and fracture strength of zirconia implant crowns
summary: Researchers tested 72 implant-supported monolithic zirconia crowns divided into six groups, varying whether a screw access hole was present, its diameter (1, 2 or 3 mm), and whether it was made before or after cementation. Crowns without an access hole had larger marginal and internal discrepancies than those with one, and fracture loads were higher without a hole or with a 1-mm hole than with 2- or 3-mm openings. Handpiece-prepared groups showed lower Weibull moduli, while for 3-mm holes the preparation method did not change mean fracture load.

headline: Systematic review finds AI in pre-implant imaging strongest for anatomical analysis
summary: This systematic review of 36 studies from 2021 to 2025 assessed AI applied to radiographic imaging before dental implant placement, with CBCT being the most common modality. AI performed well on segmentation and anatomical analysis tasks, while positional accuracy and planning outcomes varied more. Risk of bias was high in most of the studies that could be assessed, so the authors synthesized findings qualitatively.
why: AI tools may help with anatomical assessment and save workflow time before implant surgery, but autonomous implant positioning and outcome prediction are not yet supported well enough, so clinician oversight remains essential.

headline: Risk factors for peri-implant disease change over 10 years with laser-microgrooved implants
summary: A retrospective study reviewed records of 60 patients with 240 implants having laser micro-grooved collars, followed for 10 years in a private practice under preventive maintenance. Peri-implant health stayed the same in 42% of cases, worsened in 36%, and improved in 22%. Periodontitis history, plaque, cleaning difficulty, smoking, systemic disease, a 30° prosthetic emergence angle, and cemented crowns were linked to worsening, and the authors concluded that modifiable patient, prosthetic and maintenance factors drive disease progression.
why: It suggests that clinicians can influence long-term implant health by managing modifiable risks such as plaque control, smoking, systemic conditions, and prosthetic design, supporting personalized maintenance plans.

headline: Flapless, immediately loaded mini-implants retain complete overdentures over 24 months
summary: A single-center prospective study followed 25 fully edentulous patients whose complete dentures were converted chairside into implant-retained overdentures using flaplessly placed, one-piece mini-implants loaded immediately. Of 158 mini-implants placed (120 maxillary, 38 mandibular), 145 remained in function at 24 months, an implant-level survival of 91.8%. Bone loss and peri-implant attachment loss were limited, with greater attachment loss in the maxilla.
why: This minimally invasive option may give dentists another way to improve denture retention in edentulous patients, including those with narrow ridges or who are reluctant to undergo augmentation, though the study is a single-center cohort.

headline: In silico survey maps ABC transporters in five endodontic pathogens
summary: Researchers computationally characterised ATP-binding cassette transporter proteins across five endodontic pathogens using reference genome data from NCBI RefSeq. They identified 574 such proteins, with multidrug resistance pumps forming the largest functional group, and found significant differences between species in physicochemical properties. In E. faecalis, sequence analysis confirmed the efrAB efflux operon along with 13 homologue proteins.
why: The study suggests multidrug efflux pumps in E. faecalis could provide a molecular basis for intrinsic resistance to intracanal medicaments in persistent endodontic infections, though this is a computational finding and not yet clinical evidence.

headline: Genetic study links malocclusion, but not dental attrition, to temporomandibular disorders
summary: Using a two-sample Mendelian randomization design with European genome-wide association data, researchers tested whether malocclusion and dental attrition independently cause temporomandibular disorders (TMDs). Genetic liability to malocclusion showed a strong association with TMD risk after accounting for shared genetic factors, while attrition did not show an independent direct effect.
why: The findings suggest malocclusion may be an independent risk factor for TMDs, which could inform how clinicians assess patients with TMD symptoms, though the study is genetic-based and does not itself establish treatment outcomes.

headline: Surface texture and depth tuned for bonding and strength of 3D printed zirconia crowns
summary: An in vitro study tested nanoparticle jetting (NPJ) 3D printed zirconia with four surface textures and four depths, comparing them with milled zirconia. Textured surfaces increased bond strength, with circular and undercut circular patterns performing best, and bond strength plateaued at 80 to 100 μm. Across the tested designs, a 60-μm circular texture gave the best balance of bond strength and fracture resistance for 0.5-mm ultrathin crowns.
why: It suggests that specific intaglio surface designs could help ultrathin printed zirconia crowns bond well without losing fracture resistance, though these are lab results that still need clinical validation.

headline: Zygomatic implants vs. other fixed options for the atrophic maxilla: systematic review
summary: A systematic review compared zygomatic implant fixed rehabilitation with other fixed implant-supported approaches for the atrophic edentulous maxilla, based on five RCTs and one observational study. Zygomatic implants were associated with better oral health-related quality of life than All-on-4, and with fewer implant failures than bone augmentation, though biological complications were higher with zygomatic implants in that comparison. The certainty of evidence was rated low to very low across outcomes.
why: For clinicians treating severely atrophic upper jaws, zygomatic implants may offer quality-of-life and implant-survival benefits, but the weak evidence means treatment choice should remain a shared, case-by-case decision with patients.

headline: Deep learning measures dental plaque in disclosed photos, agreeing with clinical scoring
summary: Researchers tested a deep-learning system that measures buccal plaque coverage from disclosed intraoral photographs of 20 adults taken after 48 hours without oral hygiene. The automated coverage scores ranked teeth similarly to a calibrated dentist's Turesky-modified Quigley-Hein index scores, and after threshold calibration agreement matched that between two examiners. The authors suggest the tool could act as an auxiliary second opinion, pending external validation.

headline: Unified Brazilian Child Perceptions Questionnaire validated for ages 5-14
summary: Researchers developed and validated a single Brazilian Portuguese version of the Child Perceptions Questionnaire covering children aged 5 to 14, built from common and age-specific items of the existing 8-10 and 11-14 versions. In a sample of 200 children and their parents or caregivers, the instrument showed good internal consistency, high test-retest reliability, and convergent and discriminant validity, including differences between children with and without dental caries. Factor analyses supported a unidimensional structure that fit better than a four-factor model.

headline: Additive SLA workflow gave better internal fit for inlay-retained fixed partial dentures
summary: An in vitro study compared the fit accuracy of inlay-retained fixed partial dentures made by two additive manufacturing workflows (SLA and DLP) and one subtractive milling workflow, using typodont mandibular premolar and molar abutments. Fit was measured in 3D by comparing scans, with internal and marginal deviations quantified. The additive SLA workflow showed superior internal trueness and less variability in internal fit, while marginal fit was comparable across groups.
why: Suggests that the manufacturing workflow chosen for inlay-retained bridges may affect internal adaptation, though the findings come from a laboratory typodont study and do not yet establish clinical outcomes.

headline: Extraoral scanbody workflow beats intraoral scanbodies in complete-arch in vitro test
summary: An in vitro study compared an extraoral GeoXact scanbody workflow with a conventional intraoral scanbody workflow for transferring positions of implants in a complete arch. Using a maxillary edentulous cast with six digital analogs scanned 15 times per workflow, the extraoral method showed smaller translational deviation, lower global surface deviation, and smaller angular deviation. The authors say these are metrological results that still need prosthetic-fit and clinical validation.

headline: AI score from panoramic X-rays linked to five major systemic diseases
summary: A retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 26,550 panoramic radiographs from two hospitals using AI that detected teeth and implants and measured alveolar bone loss. It produced a 0-100 score based on missing teeth and weighted bone-loss severity. Patients with diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis, ischemic heart disease, or hyperlipidemia had lower scores than controls, and the score stayed independently associated with all five conditions after adjustment, though it added significant discrimination only for diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia.
why: Routinely taken panoramic radiographs may eventually offer an automated, exploratory marker that signals systemic disease risk and supports coordination between dental and medical care, though the study is retrospective and not yet a clinical tool.

headline: Survey finds posterior resin composite teaching is established in Indonesian dental schools
summary: A cross-sectional study emailed a 23-item questionnaire to faculty at all 38 Indonesian dental schools, with an 84% response rate, about how posterior composites are taught. All responding schools taught occlusal and two- and three-surface occluso-proximal composite restorations in premolars and molars. Most schools taught removal of residual caries before restoration, and many taught composites ahead of amalgam, though amalgam was still taught first at more schools than composites.
why: It offers a snapshot of how future dentists are trained in direct posterior composites and suggests amalgam teaching is gradually declining, which may shape the restorative skills new graduates bring to practice.

headline: Dental wear studies need consistent methods to link lab results with clinical performance
summary: A Short Communication in the Journal of Dentistry argues that dental wear research is methodologically inconsistent, which makes it hard to compare studies or relate lab findings to clinical outcomes. It reviews wear protocols, digital measurement workflows, and outcome measures such as vertical loss, volumetric loss, antagonist wear, and structural damage. The authors conclude that no single universal wear-testing protocol fits every question, and that experimental design should match the research question and be validated against clinical evidence.
why: Dentists should be cautious about applying laboratory wear results to patients, since the choice of test protocol and measurement method can change what the findings mean.

headline: Regular formative testing lifts short-term macroscopic anatomy scores in dental students
summary: A study of second-year dental students at the University of Oslo compared two groups: one with standard teaching only, and one that also completed three mandatory formative assessments during a 6-week anatomy module. The testing group scored markedly higher on a 150-task test right after teaching, with the biggest gains in myology and neurology. By the final practical exam four weeks later, the testing group still generally scored higher, though the initial gap had narrowed.

headline: Dental marketing should start with practice identity, not websites or ads
summary: An episode of the Dentistry Unmasked podcast features Grace Rizza, CEO of Identity Dental Marketing, discussing marketing. The conversation argues that effective marketing begins well before a website is built, social media is posted to, or an ad campaign is launched.
why: It suggests practices should define their brand identity first, so that websites, social posts and ads are built on a clear foundation rather than used in isolation.

headline: VCS Medical launches DentalJect drug-free topical spray to ease injection pain
summary: VCS Medical announced the full US market launch of DentalJect, a drug-free topical anesthetic spray meant to reduce pain and anxiety during dental injections. The company says the spray numbs the injection site in seconds, so clinicians can inject right away without waiting. The release cites an estimated 25% of adults and up to 75% of children as having fear of injections.
why: A topical that numbs in seconds could shorten chair time and make injection-anxious patients more willing to accept needed treatment, though the claims come from the manufacturer's release and have not been independently verified here.
